tagline: A memory organ for AI agents. Long-term recall and an entity graph that any agent reaches over MCP — so what one session learns, the next one already knows.

lines.text: hybrid recall · vector + BM25 · RRF · reranked

cards.title: Hybrid recall, not just vectors
cards.copy: Vector similarity and BM25 fused with reciprocal rank, then reranked. A name or an exact phrase is found by the half of the search that is good at names.

cards.title: Hot and cold, like a brain
cards.copy: A hippocampal hot tier answers fast; a cortical cold tier keeps everything. Salience-gated consolidation moves what matters between them while you are not looking.

cards.title: Reconsolidation on recall
cards.copy: Remembering something changes it — recall strengthens a memory and lets it be corrected, rather than leaving a stale fact to be retrieved for ever.

cards.title: Any client, one protocol
cards.copy: Claude Code and Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor connect through the zekra CLI. Claude.ai and ChatGPT connect to the remote server at mcp.zekra.dev and sign in with OAuth — no local binary.

cards.title: Every memory is a note
cards.copy: What an agent retains is a note you can read, tag, link and edit in the console — and every note is a node in the brain's entity graph.

cards.title: Scoped brains and a secrets vault
cards.copy: Each brain is granted per agent and per person, with scoped tokens. A credential pasted into a memory is moved into an encrypted vault instead of being stored as text.

steps.title: Log in with a token from the console
Or add it to Claude.ai or ChatGPT
steps.copy: Add a custom connector with this URL and sign in with your Zekra account.

closing.title: Status
closing.copy: Live. The console runs at app.zekra.dev and the remote MCP server at mcp.zekra.dev, on Postgres with VectorChord and BM25, embedding and reranking through TEI — retain, recall, notes and the entity graph are in daily use.

cta.title: Give your agents a memory.
cta.copy: Open the console to create a brain, mint a scoped token and connect Claude Code, Cursor, Claude.ai, ChatGPT or any MCP client.

explainer.title: Why Zekra?
explainer.note: Four ways an agent can know something, from the shortest-lived to the longest.
explainer.diagram:
conversation history   one session       lost when the context resets
        ↓
traditional RAG        documents         retrieved, but the agent cannot write back
        ↓
persistent memory      what it learned   retained now, recalled next session
        ↓
Zekra                  memory + graph    hybrid recall · entities · tiers · over MCP

items.title: Conversation history
items.copy: Everything the agent knows lives in the context window, and goes when the session ends or the window fills.

items.title: Traditional RAG
items.copy: Retrieval over documents someone indexed. Useful for reference material; the agent reads it but does not add to it.

items.title: Persistent memory
items.copy: The agent retains decisions and facts as it works, and recalls them in a later session — so the second session starts where the first ended.

items.title: Zekra
items.copy: Persistent memory with an entity graph, vector + BM25 recall and hot/cold tiers, behind MCP tools. Connectors still ingest text, markdown, GitHub, SQL and crawled pages — RAG sits inside it, not against it.

presentations.title: Turn what your team knows into decks, reports and pages — Arabic and English
presentations.copy: The memory your agents build is also your team's. Zekra presentations start from a note, a recall query or a whole brain and draft a customer-ready deck, report or landing page from what the brain actually holds.

cards.title: From notes and brains
cards.copy: Pick notes, a query or a brain; the draft is built from those memories, not from a blank page.

cards.title: Deck, report or page
cards.copy: One source, three shapes: slides to present, a report to send, a page to publish.

cards.title: Arabic and English
cards.copy: Right-to-left Arabic is laid out properly, not mirrored as an afterthought.

cards.title: PDF and Word
cards.copy: Export a deck or report as PDF or as an editable Word document.

cards.title: Private share links
cards.copy: Share with a customer by link; the link is the only key, and you can revoke it.

cards.title: Owned by the brain
cards.copy: Presentations live with the brain they came from, under the same access grants.
